On the 19th November we had Woodford Green A.C. and the Royal Military Police (Woking) as visitors to Belgrave Hall, for an 8 aside match over our 5 miles cross-country course. Bromley of the Police was first man home just in front of Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown.
Whitlock, of Walton, was first man home in 28.54 and our placings and times were: 6, Charlton, 29.49; 8, Brown, 29.56; 9, Davies, 29.59; 11, Towndrow, 30.24; 19, England, 31.48.

…o finished in front of him, including the Pirie brothers, Chataway of Walton, who won the recent South of Thames event, Brown of Mitcham who was runner-up in the National Youth's race, and Green of Reading who gave Len Marchant a start and beating in last year's London to Brighton Relay race.…

At the half-distance there was a group of four runners with Brown, Blowfield, Bill Lucas and Steve Charlton all nicely together in under the half-hour, which is good running for our five miles course.
Derrick Burfitt was not defending his 1 mile Senior title and Jack Brown ran a good race to beat Len Herbert with Bob Taylor gaining his first club championship medal in third place.

Brown, the Mitcham lad, who won the recent South of Thames race, Bowen, of the local club, Nicholson, of Woodford Green, a most experienced runner, and Culver, of Essex Beagles, who last year was credited with the fastest lap time.

The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas.

Smart regained one place and then Jack Brown, with the second fastest time of the day, brought us back to 4th. Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day.

The bulk of our supporters had, by then, assembled on the Common at Mitcham and only Walker and Brown had so far failed to report. The team was not quite as planned as Jumbo Masters still had an injured leg , so Charlie Smart was moved and Eric Gebbett brought into the team.

Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of…

The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.

Pride of place goes to Jack Brown for his excellent run on the seventh leg which gave him a stage record. This was made with no help whatsoever as the team in front were well out of sight for most of the leg and those behind were never with Jack.

Middle distance talent is almost in abundance so with challengers like Hampshire,Jarvis, Alan Mead, Hammond, Wiseman, Brown, Yeo, Redwood and Satchell not very far behind, David cannot afford to flag in his efforts.
